title: Carrots, frozen, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Carrots, frozen, cooked with butter or margarine are a ready‑to‑eat product made from fresh carrots that are quickly frozen after being briefly cooked with butter or margarine. The process preserves the bright colour, tender texture and natural sweetness of the carrot.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Freezing retains most of the vitamins and minerals found in fresh carrots.
Cooking with butter or margarine enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A and K.
Frozen carrots are a staple ingredient in many mixed vegetable side dishes and soups.
Heat treatment softens the carrots, making them easier for children and seniors to eat.
Butter adds a richer aroma, while margarine extends shelf life.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision, immunity and skin health.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids and vitamin C protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fibre in carrots promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: Butter‑cooked versions may trigger reactions in people sensitive to milk proteins or lactose.

items.title: Higher fat content
items.content: Added butter increases the calorie density; portion control is advisable for weight‑watchers.

items.title: Sodium in margarine
items.content: Some margarines contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options if you have hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the carrots in a skillet, microwave, or steamer. They work well as a side dish for meat or fish, in vegetable stews, soups, and salads. Finish with fresh herbs, spices, or a squeeze of lemon for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen carrots in an airtight bag at –18 °C. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and store in a sealed container in the refrigerator. Do not refreeze.
